# Special-case crawlers

*Crawler* · also written special-case crawler · contractual crawlers · contractual crawler

Google crawlers for specific products under an agreement with the site (such as AdsBot), which may ignore the global robots.txt user agent.

**Glossary** (*Contractual crawlers (special-case crawlers)*): Google crawlers that serve a specific product by agreement with the crawled site, and the only Google crawlers that may ignore robots.txt; AdsBot, for example, ignores the global user agent with the ad publisher's permission.

4 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 2 shown or said at the event (2 consistent with Google docs). A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [List of Google's special-case crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-special-case-crawlers).

- [`D1-C343`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Docs: Google's crawler documentation says special-case crawlers serve specific Google products where the crawled site and the product have an agreement about the crawl process, so they may ignore robots.txt rules; AdsBot, for example, ignores the global (*) user agent with the ad publisher's permission. `[D1-C343, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-special-case-crawlers]`
- [`D1-C138`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Docs: Google's page on verifying its crawlers says Googlebot and Google's other common crawlers resolve to crawl-*.googlebot.com or geo-crawl-*.geo.googlebot.com host names, special-case crawlers to rate-limited-proxy-*.google.com and user-triggered fetchers to *.gae.googleusercontent.com or google-proxy-*.google.com, and it publishes each group's IP ranges as JSON files such as common-crawlers.json and special-crawlers.json. `[D1-C138, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/verify-google-requests]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C329`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Apart from contractual crawlers, all of Google's automated crawlers obey robots.txt, which Google treats as the way site owners opt out of its crawling. `[D1-C329, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C330`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: The only Google-owned crawlers that do not obey robots.txt are contractual crawlers, which crawl a site whose owner has agreed that Google may crawl it however it likes. `[D1-C330, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
